name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Build a "prompt health score" metric that rates every prompt on clarity, specificity, and task alignment. This forces us to audit every prompt systematically and catches vague or bloated ones before they waste tokens or confuse the model. The trade-off is upfront effort to define the scoring rubric and review prompts, but it pays off by making future changes faster and more reliable.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t false positives—it’s that a weekly score turns prompts into checkboxes. A rubric can’t measure what matters: whether the prompt reliably produces the right output for the task. Instead, audit the top 20% of prompts by actual failure rate in production; that’s where the waste lives. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot on those prompts and comparing error rates before/after.
